Package nz.ac.wgtn.swen225.lc.domain

Record Class Point

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
nz.ac.wgtn.swen225.lc.domain.Point
Record Components:
x - the x-coordinate of the point
y - the y-coordinate of the point
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<Point>, JSONSerializable<Point>
public record Point(long x, long y) extends Record implements Comparable<Point>, JSONSerializable<Point>
Represents a point in a 2D space using long coordinates.

  • Method Details

    • limit

      public Point limit(Long maxAxial)
      Limits the coordinates of this point within a specified maximum axial value.

      The method ensures that the x and y coordinates of the point fall within the range of -maxAxial to maxAxial (inclusive). If a coordinate exceeds the maximum or falls below the minimum, it is adjusted to the nearest boundary value.

      Parameters:
      maxAxial - the maximum allowed value for the x and y coordinates
      Returns:
      a new Point with the limited coordinates

    • mul

      public Point mul(Point other)
      Multiplies the coordinates of this point with another point.

      This method returns a new Point where each coordinate is the product of the corresponding coordinates of this point and the provided point.

      Parameters:
      other - the point to multiply with this point
      Returns:
      a new Point with the product of the coordinates

    • mul

      public Point mul(Long multiplier)
      Multiplies the coordinates of this point with a given multiplier.

      This method returns a new Point where each coordinate is the product of the corresponding coordinates of this point and the provided multiplier.

      Parameters:
      multiplier - the multiplier to multiply with this point's coordinates
      Returns:
      a new Point with the product of the coordinates and the multiplier

    • compareTo

      public int compareTo(Point other)
      Compares this point with another point for order.

      defines a natural ordering for points. The ordering is first based on the x-coordinate, and then on the y-coordinate.

      Specified by:
      compareTo in interface Comparable<Point>
      Parameters:
      other - the point to be compared with this point
      Returns:
      an integer representing teh ordering of the points
